# Drone Photography Regulations India: Complete Legal Guide for Safe and Compliant Aerial Photography in 2025
## Understanding India's Drone Photography Legal Framework
### Key Regulatory Bodies
Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA): The primary regulatory authority responsible for drone safety and operational oversight throughout India.
Digital Sky Platform: The central online platform for all drone-related registrations, permissions, and flight clearances managed by DGCA.

## Mandatory Registration Requirements
### Digital Sky Platform Registration
You must register your drone on the Digital Sky Platform by DGCA and get a Unique Identification Number (UIN). All drones except Nano drones used for personal purposes should be registered on the DGCA's Digital Sky Platform.
Registration Process:

...

UIN Requirements: Every drone above 250 grams (micro and above) must be registered on the Digital Sky Platform. The UIN must be prominently displayed on the drone before any flight operations.

...

## No-Fly Zones and Restricted Areas
### Critical Infrastructure
Airport Restrictions:
* Delhi Indira Gandhi International Airport: Within 5 km radius restricted
* Mumbai Chhatrapati Shivaji Airport: 5 km radius no-fly zone
* Chennai International Airport: 5 km radius restriction
* All airports nationwide maintain similar restricted perimeters

...

## Permissions and Clearance Procedures
### Digital Sky Platform Process
Flight Permission Application:
* Submit detailed flight plan including location, duration, and purpose
* Specify equipment details and operator credentials
* Allow 24-48 hours for approval processing

excerpts:
# Inside the deployment of drones in Mumbai to contain COVID-19
## At the helm
None of these pilots have a drone flying licence because aviation regulator Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) hasn’t authorised any drone training agency in the country, according to Shah.

...

> Subject: Drone Pilot Authorisation for Drone Surveillance for Monitoring Coronavirus LockdownTo whomsoever it may concern,The Drone Federation of India (DFI) is authorised by the Mumbai Police to fly drones to monitor the Coronavirus Lockdown as per the permission letter attached.About Drone Federation of India

...

## Finding DGCA
According to [current drone regulations](https://www.medianama.com/2018/12/223-drones-online-registration-india/) , a clearance is required from the DGCA before each drone takes flight. Called NPNT (no permission no takeoff), it is conceptually a green signal without which drones aren’t authorised to fly.
Shah said that the Digital Sky platform, which handles this clearance, hasn’t been given that functionality yet. “As of now, we can only register pilots and drones on the portal, and you can’t get permission,” Shah said.
The government has reacted to this now, however. It has [created a portal](https://www.medianama.com/2020/05/223-govt-can-deploy-coronavirus-drone-surveillance/) specifically for government bodies to deploy drones for COVID-19 related work such as aerial surveillance and photography and for public announcements.

results.title: Mumbai Police temporarily bans drone flights - Unmanned airspace
excerpts:
# Mumbai Police temporarily bans drone flights
India’s Mumbai Police have issued a temporary ban on drone flights in the district, effective from October 31, citing terrorism concerns.
The operation of drones, remote-controlled microlight aircraft, paragliders and hot air balloons is prohibited until after November 29. The [order](https://mumbaipolice.gov.in/files/PressRelease/2737.pdf) states that “restrictions are necessary to prevent probable sabotage”.
Mumbai Police will be able to operate its own uncrewed aerial systems for surveillance and specific permission can be requested for flights.
